ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocol: Mandatory screening must be conducted against the Taiwan Ministry of Justice's list of designated individuals and entities, the United Nations Security Council consolidated list, the U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, and the European Union consolidated sanctions list. Additionally, all beneficial owners, directors, and senior officers must be screened for politically exposed persons (PEPs) using a risk-based approach, with enhanced due diligence for high-risk jurisdictions. The screening must be performed at the time of onboarding and continuously thereafter, with results documented and retained for at least five years. Any positive match must be escalated to the compliance officer and reported to the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) as required under the MLCA.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: MOEA Company Registration and Commerce Information System (https://gcis.nat.gov.tw)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Traditional Chinese. An English name may be registered as a secondary name. The name must consist of a trade name, a business type, an organization type (e.g., Limited Company), and additional words. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered name. Phonetic transliteration is permitted but must be clearly distinguishable from existing names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) within 30 days of the rejection notice. The appeal must include a detailed statement of grounds, the proposed name, and any supporting evidence. The MOEA will review the appeal and issue a decision within 60 days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may seek judicial review in the Taipei High Administrative Court. It is strongly recommended to engage local counsel to prepare and submit the appeal to ensure compliance with procedural requirements.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is generally not acceptable for a company engaged in professional services such as game art outsourcing. The tax authorities and banks require a physical address for verification, audit, and credit assessment purposes. The MOEA may accept a registered agent address, but the company must maintain a physical office for operational and regulatory compliance. Banks typically reject virtual offices for account opening, and the tax authority may impose penalties for non-compliance. Therefore, a physical office is strongly recommended.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) Verify the registered office is a real, operational location; (2) Ensure the company name is displayed at the premises; (3) Maintain records of business operations at the office; (4) Have a responsible person available during business hours. Risk: Low to moderate; unannounced inspections are rare but possible, especially if the company is flagged for non-compliance. Quantified risk: 10% probability within the first year.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act (as amended), Articles 6, 18, 128, 129, 130, 133, 151, 156, 161-2, 172, 203, 208, 216, 221 and 387; Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, Articles 3, 4, 7 and 12; and Company Registration Regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce, Company Registration Section (Taiwan).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Limited by Shares Incorporation Registration Application (Form COM-1) together with the Articles of Incorporation, Minutes of the Incorporation Meeting and Share Subscription List.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed for an ISIC 7490 professional creative service company under the Taiwan Company Act. However, the capital subscribed under the Articles of Incorporation must be fully paid by the founding shareholders and, in the case of a foreign-invested joint venture, the foreign shareholder's contribution must be remitted from abroad through a licensed Taiwan bank, converted into New Taiwan Dollars where applicable, and verified by a Taiwan-certified public accountant capital verification report. No blocked escrow account or capital quarantine arrangement is required by law for this business scope.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [SINO-FOREIGN JOINT VENTURE LIMITED], TAIWAN. RESOLVED, that the form of the Articles of Incorporation, the incorporation application, and all related formation filings of the Company be, and each is hereby, approved in all respects. RESOLVED, that the authorized share capital of the Company shall be the amount stated in the Articles of Incorporation, divided into shares with the par value and class rights set forth therein, and that the founding shareholders and the foreign corporate investor have validly subscribed for all shares allocated to them. RESOLVED, that the Chairperson and the General Manager, acting jointly, are authorized to deposit the subscribed capital into a bank account to be opened in the name of the Company and to procure from a Taiwan-certified public accountant the capital verification report required for registration. RESOLVED, that the registered office and principal place of business of the Company shall be established at [INSERT TAIWAN ADDRESS], Taiwan, and that the Chairperson is authorized to execute the office lease, obtain landlord consent, and file the registered address with the competent registry. RESOLVED, that the Company shall open one or more corporate banking accounts, including a foreign currency account, and that the banking signatory scheme shall be any two of the Chairperson, the General Manager, and the Chief Financial Officer, acting jointly, or such other scheme as the Board may subsequently approve in writing. RESOLVED, that [INSERT NAME] be and is hereby appointed Chairperson of the Board, [INSERT NAME] be and is hereby appointed General Manager, [INSERT NAME] be and is hereby appointed Supervisor, and [INSERT NAME] be and is hereby appointed Company Secretary and Compliance Officer, each to serve until the next annual general meeting of the Company. RESOLVED, that the Chairperson and the General Manager, acting jointly, are authorized to execute and file all tax registrations, labor insurance registrations, bank forms, foreign-investment declarations, and any other documents necessary to commence lawful business in Taiwan. RESOLVED, that the Board delegates to the General Manager all ordinary operational authority for the Company's ISIC 7490 game art design, 3D sculpting, character rigging, and creative process outsourcing business, subject to expenditure limits approved by the Board. RESOLVED, that these resolutions are effective immediately and shall continue in full force until amended, revoked, or superseded by a subsequent resolution of the Board of Directors. THIS RESOLUTION IS DULY ADOPTED.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce, Company Name and Business Scope Pre-approval System (Taiwan).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the pre-approval application through MOEA's online Company Name and Business Scope Pre-approval System using the shareholder's digital certificate or authorized agent credentials. The proposed name must distinguish the Company in Taiwan and avoid a name that is already registered or that misleads the public. Business scope must be drafted to reflect only professional creative services under ISIC 7490, including 3D game asset sculpting, character rigging, environment art, visual R&D, and creative process outsourcing; no manufacturing, trading, or regulated activity may be included. After electronic payment, the system produces a pre-approval certificate valid for six months.
required_dossiers: Completed online name and business scope application
Passport or national ID copies of all founding shareholders
Power of attorney if filing through a Taiwan agent
Proposed English company name and romanized Chinese name where required
Business scope narrative limited to ISIC 7490 creative services
Payment receipt for the pre-approval fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If name pre-approval is rejected for similarity or business scope ambiguity, withdraw the application and resubmit with three alternative names and a narrower ISIC 7490 service description; MOEA will re-screen the corrected application within the same statutory quarantine without a new name fee where the ground is purely descriptive.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Approval and Capital Remittance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Foreign Investment Approval Section, Taiwan.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an investment application with the Investment Commission, MOEA under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals. Describe the joint venture structure, identify each shareholder, attach the draft articles or joint venture agreement, provide evidence of financial capability and source of funds. Once approved, the Investment Commission issues an approval letter which is required for the foreign shareholder to remit equity. After issuance, the foreign shareholder must remit the subscribed capital through a licensed bank in Taiwan and obtain a foreign exchange transaction certificate and bank deposit certificate. The remittance must be completed before company registration and must be included in the CPA capital verification report.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Application Form
Approved company name and business scope certificate
Draft Articles of Incorporation or joint venture agreement
Passports and corporate registration certificates of all shareholders
Bank references and source-of-funds statement
Power of attorney for the Taiwan resident agent
Pro forma share subscription and capital contribution schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the approval is suspended for missing legalization, the foreign shareholder must notarize and legalize the relevant documents through the Taipei representative office or an apostille-competent authority and resubmit. If the proposed ownership ratio or business scope is questioned, amend the shareholding schedule or submit a supplemental scope explanation to the Investment Commission for reconsideration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce, One-Stop Company Registration System (Taiwan).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation registration application and all required attachments to the MOEA Department of Commerce through the one-stop online company registration system. The registry will examine the Articles of Incorporation, the minutes of the incorporation meeting, the share subscription list, the capital verification report issued by a Taiwan CPA, the registered office consent, and the foreign investment approval. The officers must certify under penalty of law that the information is complete and accurate. Once the application is approved, the Company will be entered into the company register and issued its Certificate of Incorporation and unified company registration number. A company comes into legal existence as a juristic person upon registration.
required_dossiers: Company Incorporation Registration Application (Form COM-1)
Articles of Incorporation duly signed by shareholders
Minutes of the incorporation meeting
Share subscription and allotment list
CPA capital verification report
Registered office lease, landlord consent, or certificate of address
Consent forms of directors, chairperson, supervisor and general manager
Foreign Investment Approval Letter
IDs of directors and shareholders
Company chop or seal specimen
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOEA issues a correction notice, cure the deficiency within fifteen days and resubmit the corrected signature page. If registration is suspended due to substantive legal defects, the shareholders and directors must adopt a remedial board resolution approving amended Articles and then file an amendment registration. An adverse rejection may be appealed to the Ministry of Economic Affairs within the statutory appeal period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Labor, Banking and Premises-Use Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance; Bureau of Labor Insurance, Ministry of Labor; local municipal government for premises use; licensed Taiwan bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after incorporation, apply to the National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance, for tax registration and a uniform invoice number. Register the Company as an employer with the Bureau of Labor Insurance, Ministry of Labor, before hiring staff. Open permanent NT dollar and foreign currency current accounts at the chosen bank and deposit the verified paid-in capital. Confirm with the local municipal government that the office premises are lawfully zoned for professional services. Because the business is an office-based ISIC 7490 creative service, no factory registration, environmental impact assessment, or Civil Defense fire permit is triggered.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Company registration number certificate
Company chop and resolution opening bank accounts
Capital verification report
Foreign Investment Approval Letter
Office lease and landlord building-use certificate
Passport or ID copies of approved signatories
Tax registration application form
Labor insurance and health insurance employer enrollment forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is delayed, request expedited handling from the National Taxation Bureau and continue operations only after receiving the uniform invoice number. If the premises-use certificate is insufficient, obtain a zoning or building-use verification from the municipal authority before commencing office operations. Late labor insurance enrollment must be cured immediately and, where statute permits, with retrospective employer election to avoid employee coverage gaps.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable — ISIC 7490 is a non-manufacturing professional creative service; no industrial licensing board is engaged.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable — no factory, chemical plant, assembly line, or warehousing operation is licensed.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable — the Environmental Protection Administration (Taiwan) has no jurisdiction over an office-based 3D game art outsourcing service.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not Applicable — no EIA screening, no full or partial EIA report, and no installation air-pollution registration is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable — no industrial wastewater, volatile organic compound emission source, hazardous waste stream, or regulated discharge is generated; ordinary office waste is managed through municipal waste systems.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable — no Civil Defense fire permit is triggered for office-only use. The commercial office must nevertheless maintain a valid building-use and fire safety inspection record satisfying local Fire Bureau regulations and must complete a workplace safety self-inspection under the Occupational Safety and Health Act before employees commence duties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and its administrative arm, the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The RMB is fully convertible for eligible current-account transactions, including trade in services and recurring service fees, subject to genuine-transaction documentation and bank-based verification. Capital-account convertibility remains restricted: all cross-border equity investment, shareholder loans, and capital injections must be registered with SAFE through the Direct Investment Management System before funds are admitted into the PRC. For a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture, dividend and profit remittance to a Taiwan shareholder is treated as a current-account transaction or as remittance of lawful earnings, permitted after annual audit completion, corporate income tax clearance, and the submission of the SAFE Foreign Exchange Registration for Direct Investment. The primary hurdles are (i) proof of authenticity through invoices, tax certificates, and audited financial statements; (ii) SAFE registration of each capital-account movement; and (iii) compliance with the Negative List, which does not restrict 3D game art outsourcing but may require disclaimers on content production and data security.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The PRC abolished mandatory surrender of export proceeds in 2012. Export-related receipts, including cross-border payments for 3D art asset creation, character rigging, and related BPO services, must be repatriated to a domestic bank account through a licensed settlement bank. The exporter or service provider may retain the foreign currency in a current-account foreign exchange settlement account or convert it to RMB at market rate. Statutory verification: export and service receipts must be matched and verified via SAFE's 'Trade Foreign Exchange Receipt and Payment Monitoring System' within the prescribed timelines, generally 30 days for advance payments and 90 days for ordinary shipment or service completion receipts. No minimum conversion ratio applies, but every inbound remittance must bear a clear service description and be declared under the correct SAFE trade-in-services code.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium. Offshore digital EMI platforms (e.g., Payoneer, Wise Business, PayPal Business) are not licensed banks in the PRC and cannot serve as the primary treasury vehicle. They may be used as auxiliary collection channels for low-value overseas clients, but every receivable derived from export of services must ultimately be routed into an onshore bank account subject to SAFE monitoring. Legal constraints: the JV must not hold operating receivables offshore; any funds parked with an unlicensed EMI will create a false declaration issue and may trigger AML scrutiny for unverified cross-border receipts. The only robust use for these EMIs is inbound connectivity to a Chinese settlement bank through an approved payment aggregator, with full underlying contract and tax invoice flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory for the legal representative and at least one authorized director of the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture during the bank account opening interview at the PRC branch of the chosen bank. Remote opening is generally not permitted for foreign-invested enterprises. If the Taiwan shareholder's appointed director cannot travel, the director may be represented by a power-of-attorney that is notarized in Taiwan and authenticated by the relevant cross-strait document verification process, with the attorney physically present. The legal representative must produce original passport or PRC ID, business license, Articles of Association, the SAFE FDI registration certificate, and evidence of the registered address. A site visit by the bank's compliance officer to the registered office may also be required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Incomplete or opaque disclosure of the beneficial ownership chain, especially when the Taiwan shareholder is a holding company or an offshore trust.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a certified org chart from the ultimate individual beneficial owner to the PRC JV; register certificates of ultimate beneficial owners in the bank's AML system; include the Taiwan entity's audited financial statements, business license, minutes of shareholders' meetings, and notarized statements confirming no government ownership or sanctioned-party ties; and provide a written explanation of the funding pathway for each capital contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Use of PayPal or other digital EMI for B2B trade invoicing, causing a mismatch between declared service export code and payment channel profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply the complete client contracts, work orders for 3D asset creation, delivery logs, invoice and payment routing matrix, and an explanation that PayPal is used only as an invoicing convenience for small-ticket overseas clients. Confirm in writing that all proceeds are repatriated within the statutory verification window and that no digital EMI holds corporate funds overnight for treasury purposes. Include the bank's own FATCA and CRS forms to demonstrate tax transparency.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Cross-border receipts denominated in USD or EUR for gaming art outsource services where the industry code (ISIC 7490) could be perceived as intangible software licensing instead of professional BPO services.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide detailed time-and-material or per-deliverable cost breakdown, signed SOWs, project asset inventories, and a 'Master Service Agreement' explicitly describing the supply of digital art assets, rigging, and character design, with neither ownership of IP nor software licensing being assigned to the Chinese entity. Add a certified statement from the tax advisor explaining why the receipts are service income, not royalty or license income, and provide SAFE service trade declaration codes consistent with the 7490 scope.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Capital injection from a Taiwan entity into a Chinese JV without clear proof of the source-of-funds in the Taiwan entity's bank account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide bank statements of the Taiwan investing entity for at least six months, audited financial statements, tax filings proving lawful accumulation of the capital, a board resolution from the Taiwan entity approving the investment, and a certified certificate of deposit or asset valuation letter. Where funds originate from a third-party lender, provide the executed loan agreement, the lender's due-diligence pack, and the on-lending structure to the JV, with an explanation of the interest rate and repayment terms.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements, business report, and profit distribution/loss compensation proposal acknowledged at the annual shareholders meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commercial Affairs; filing required only where the Company Act threshold is met or MOEA orders a filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than six months after fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year company, by 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Responsible persons are subject to administrative fines under the Company Act for failure to prepare and obtain acknowledgment of financial statements; continued non-compliance may trigger a compulsory filing order from MOEA; administrative dissolution or strike-off may occur if the company does not commence business within six months or ceases business for more than one year.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-seeking enterprise income tax annual return and self-assessment tax payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance (jurisdictionally competent tax office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 May of the year following the tax year; calendar-year taxpayer basis
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing and late-payment penalties accrue monthly by reference to the assessed or unpaid tax; understatement penalties may reach double the underpaid tax in cases of intentional tax evasion; tax authorities may issue official assessments and enforce compulsory collection; sustained failure to file or pay can result in cancellation of tax registration and administrative business deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual operational implementation report filed by the approved foreign-invested equity joint venture
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEAIC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the close of the fiscal year and in the form stipulated in the foreign investment approval letter; normally by 30 June for a calendar-year company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The foreign investment approval may be suspended or revoked for material false reporting or continued failure to file; such revocation may impair dividend repatriation, capital withdrawal, and other foreign-investor rights; administrative strike-off is not a direct consequence, but loss of foreign investment approval may trigger MOEA deregistration procedures.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent CPA audit applies when the company's paid-in capital reaches the MOEA-published threshold of NT$30 million for companies limited by shares; MOEA may also require audited financial statements for smaller companies where necessary. For this JV, audit is compulsory only if the paid-in capital threshold is met or the foreign-investment approval letter imposes audited reporting conditions.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Non-public Taiwanese companies apply the Business Entity Accounting Act and related accounting treatment regulations (local GAAP); public companies and companies electing IFRS apply Taiwan-IFRS as endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan does not impose a standalone annual public UBO confirmation filing. The JV must maintain an up-to-date register of members at the registered office, and any share transfer or pledge is effective against the company only after registration in the share register. For foreign-invested JVs, changes in foreign investor equity or control must be reported to the MOEA Investment Commission in accordance with the approval conditions; there is no fixed annual UBO refresh deadline, but ownership information must be accurate and available for inspection by competent authorities.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$2,500–US$6,000 per engagement if the audit threshold is met
